developments: The Nasdaq fell as much as 2% in the US session as chip stocks slid again ahead of Nvidia's results, while bitcoin held near $64,650 on Kraken, little changed from the morning edition.
Crypto shares took the brunt: Coinbase fell about 6% and Strategy about 7% by 15:09 UTC, cryptoticker reported from Yahoo Finance data.
Zcash dropped to about $846 on Kraken as the coinholder vote on Zcash Community Grants opened, before recovering to near $883.
briefing.changed: Bitcoin barely moved from $64,500 at the morning edition to about $64,650, after a session low near $63,840 and a brief spike to $65,630 around the US open. What changed is US stocks: the Asian chip sell-off spread to Wall Street and crypto shares fell much harder than bitcoin itself.
briefing.question: Can bitcoin keep holding above $62,000 if Nvidia's results on Tuesday night extend the tech sell-off?
briefing.watch: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at a San Francisco Fed hearing on AI and productivity from about 17:00 UK, then Monday's ETF flows after the 21:00 UK close. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Wall Street's tech slide deepens as bitcoin holds its ground
lead.standfirst: The Nasdaq fell up to 2% as chip stocks extended their losses before Nvidia's results, but bitcoin held near $64,600 while crypto shares sank.
body: US technology shares fell sharply on Monday as the sell-off in Asian chipmakers spread to Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite was down 1.98% at 15:09 UTC, according to Yahoo Finance data cited by cryptoticker, after Reuters reported a fall of more than 1% at the open.

Nvidia shed about 2% ahead of its third-quarter results on Tuesday, its first since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. The Financial Times reported that Huang and allies were discussing a campaign to reinstate him, and President Trump said bringing him back "certainly isn't a bad idea", Yahoo Finance reported.

Bitcoin held up better than shares. It traded near $64,650 on Kraken at 16:30 UK, about where it stood in the morning, after dipping to about $63,840 shortly before midday UK and briefly touching $65,630 around the US open. Crypto stocks fell harder, with Coinbase down about 6% and Strategy about 7%.

Options traders are leaning defensive. The $60,000 put is now the largest bitcoin options position on Deribit, at about $900 million in notional value, overtaking the $100,000 call, CoinDesk reported. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index stood at 10, extreme fear.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attends a San Francisco Fed hearing on AI and productivity this evening, UK time, and US spot bitcoin ETF flows for Monday follow after the close.

headline: The Nasdaq fell up to 2% and crypto stocks sank as the AI sell-off spread to Wall Street, but bitcoin held near $64,650. Zcash dipped to about $846 as its grants vote opened before recovering.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, afternoon edition. The tech sell-off reached Wall Street, with the Nasdaq down as much as two percent ahead of Nvidia's results on Tuesday night. Coinbase fell about six percent and Strategy about seven. Bitcoin held up better, near sixty-four thousand six hundred and fifty dollars, little changed since the morning. The biggest bitcoin options bet is now a fall below sixty thousand. Zcash dipped to about eight hundred and forty-six dollars as its community grants vote opened, then recovered to around eight hundred and eighty. Fed Chair Warsh speaks at a San Francisco Fed hearing from about five this evening, and ETF flows follow after nine. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Chip sell-off spreads to Wall Street; Nasdaq down up to 2%
stories.why: The Nasdaq fell more than 1% at the open, Reuters reported, and was down 1.98% at 15:09 UTC with the S&P 500 down 1.24%, according to Yahoo Finance data cited by cryptoticker. Nvidia slipped about 2% before Tuesday's results; the FT reported Jensen Huang's allies were discussing his return, and Trump said that "certainly isn't a bad idea". The VIX rose about 8% to near 21.
stories.caveat: Index levels moved through the session; later Yahoo readings showed the Nasdaq down about 1.4%.

note.read: The Asian chip selling was not a one-off: US tech is now trading defensively into Nvidia, which keeps the main pressure on risk assets including crypto.
note.alt: Some of the move may be positioning before a known event, which can reverse sharply once results are out.
note.change: A steady Nvidia report and a Nasdaq rebound on Wednesday would ease this pressure.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $64,650 while crypto stocks sink
stories.why: Bitcoin traded between about $63,840 and $65,630 on Kraken since midnight and stood near $64,650 at 16:30 UK, against $64,500 at the morning edition. Coinbase fell about 6.3% and Strategy about 7.4% by 15:09 UTC, cryptoticker reported. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index was at 10, extreme fear.

note.read: Bitcoin holding flat while the Nasdaq fell 2% suggests some selling has already been done; crypto shares carried the risk-off move today.
note.alt: Bitcoin may simply be lagging, as it did last week, and could catch down if US selling continues into the close.
note.change: A drop through the session low near $63,840 or a fresh ETF outflow print tonight would weaken that reading.

stories.title: Biggest bitcoin options bet is now a fall below $60,000
stories.why: The $60,000 put on Deribit has about $900 million of notional open interest, overtaking the $100,000 call at $867 million as upside bets were closed, CoinDesk reported. A large trader has rolled puts down from $74,000 to $63,000 strikes, per Paradigm. Implied volatility (Volmex BVIV) spiked to 57 at the weekend and eased to 44.
stories.caveat: Open interest builds over months, so the $60,000 put partly reflects older hedges rather than fresh bearish bets.

note.read: Hedging is concentrated between $60,000 and $68,000, so that range is where options activity could amplify moves.
note.alt: Easing implied volatility suggests fear has cooled since the weekend low.
note.change: A renewed spike in implied volatility alongside a break below $62,000.

stories.title: Zcash dips to about $846 as the grants vote opens
stories.why: Zcash touched about $846 on Kraken and stood near $883 at 16:30 UK. The non-binding vote, open until 30 November 23:59 UTC, centres on moving 50,000 ZEC from the Zcash Community Grants treasury to the Network Sustainability Mechanism, which pays it back to miners over years, cryptoticker reported. Any change would need the NU7.1 upgrade.
stories.caveat: CoinGecko showed a midday low near $860; cryptoticker says the vote coincided with the drop but is not confirmed as its cause.

stories.title: Luxor patches attack that redirected miners' bitcoin rewards
stories.why: Attackers used Luxor's Commander software to redirect payouts from just over a dozen customer machines, sending about 0.243 BTC (about $15,700) to an address, CoinDesk and The Block reported. Luxor patched it within about two hours and will reimburse customers. No effect on the Bitcoin network itself.

stories.title: Two firms now control about 29% of Zcash hashrate
stories.why: Fortitude Mining (about 5.4 GSol/s) and Cypherpunk Technologies (about 4.2 GSol/s) together hold roughly 29% of the network's estimated 33 GSol/s, TokenPost reported. Concentration matters as miners help set the date for the NU7.1 upgrade.

stories.title: ETF outflow streak still awaits Monday's data
stories.why: No new flow data since the morning. Spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $2.35 billion over two weeks, according to SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk. Monday's figures land after the 21:00 UK close.

explained.title: Why crypto shares fall harder than bitcoin
body: Companies such as Coinbase and Strategy are listed shares, so they are sold along with the rest of the stock market on days like this. Their earnings or balance sheets also depend on crypto prices and trading volumes, which adds a layer of leverage on top of bitcoin's own move.

So a 1% move in bitcoin can come with a 6% or 7% move in these shares, as happened today. A large gap like this shows the selling is coming from stock-market investors rather than from bitcoin holders.

investigating: Will ETF outflows run to an eighth day? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue figures for Monday 16 November after the US close.
Did the Zcash grants vote cause today's dip? Evidence: vote participation updates on the Zcash forum and whether ZEC tracks bitcoin from here.
